I've finished checking: the round-2 candidate meets the Work Order and I found nothing blocking. Two advisories are below.

On an unknown total (`-1`, missing, non-integer or bool), the read keeps going until it gets a short or empty page. It can't loop forever: a full page that adds no new id fails with `list_stalled`, and so does reaching 10,000 pages, which I confirmed with a fake server that never stops. The read is still GET only. A known total is now stricter than before, not weaker. No write, retry or delete code changed, all four changed files are on the allowlist, and the diff adds no secret, IP or email address.

```

FINDING known-total-request-shape advisory: the WO says "with a non-negative total, the existing behaviour is unchanged" and "no other client behaviour changes", but round 2 also changes requests and results when the total is known: every page now sends orderBy=id&order=asc, rows are de-duplicated by id, a row without a string id fails with list_failed, a page that adds no new id fails with list_stalled, and the 10,000-page cap applies to known totals too | evidence: load/lib/crm_load/api.py:61-82 (lines 61-62 and 81-82 raise list_stalled, line 76 raises list_failed, lines 64-65 add the ordering to every query); TestListPagingSafety.test_server_ignoring_offset_known_total_is_list_stalled | expected: these all make the read stricter (the reference client scripts/crm_api.py:109 already sends the same ordering) and the tester's round-1 advisories asked for them. The PL should accept them as within the WO, or the WO should say so. A2 (operator) also checks this live on 10.0.12.

Reverting the fix therefore breaks almost every load test for a mechanical reason | evidence: base api.py with the candidate tests: "FAILED (errors=135)" out of 218 | expected: a targeted mutation is cleaner evidence (see EVIDENCE: it gives 13 relevant failures).
